ops.help: Close the editor: stop the session (the scene paused), answer, then quit
ops.name: app_quit

ops.args: {kind?: rotary|linear, a: int, b?: int, axis?: [x,y,z], anchor?: [x,y,z]}
ops.help: Join two shapes with a motor in one step: a hinge (rotary) or a slider (linear) along a world axis, put where they meet (anchor: else between their nearest points), with a servo tuned to what it carries - it holds the pose it is made in, drooping a degree at most, critically damped. Then assembly_drive target turns or slides it. Geometry alone becomes a body (the note says)
ops.name: assembly_actuator

ops.args: {name?: str, file?: str, text?: str, position?: [x,y,z], overrides?: [{name: str, line: str, key?: str, values?: []}]}
ops.help: An assembly put into the scene in one step: by its name (assembly_list), a file, or text - blocks of the scene file as scene_get gives them, with ids of their own (unused ones are given: whatever refers to whatever inside keeps doing so) - so a whole robot of shapes, joints, drives, sensors and a controller is one call. Under a group of its name standing at position (none: the origin) - the group moves and turns it whole. Answers the group's id and each id of the text with the one it got. overrides: its parts changed as it goes in, each a scene_set by the part's name - {name: "Батарея 1", line: cells, key: parallel, values: [2]} - so a ready robot takes another battery, motor or panel in the same call
ops.name: assembly_add

overrides.description: [{name: str, line: str, key?: str, values?: []}]

ops.args: {target: int, face: '+x'..'-z', joint?: 'hinge'|'weld'|'slider'|'ball'|'cylinder'|'universal'|'planar', axis?: 0|1|2, size?: [x,y,z], name?: str}
ops.help: A new link against a face of the target, joined to it at the face's centre (the magnet's click). axis: 0 and 1 across the face, 2 along its normal (a wheel); the answer gives the joint's axis in the world. Answers id (the new link, as entity) and joint
ops.name: assembly_attach

ops.args: {target?: int, face?: '+x'..'-z', point?: [x,y,z], normal?: [x,y,z], position?: [x,y,z], look_at?: [x,y,z], model?: str, name?: str, baseline?: m (0.10), fov?: degrees (65), width?: px (320), height?: px (240)}
ops.help: A stereo camera with a body of its own, as one is bought: the housing (model: an OBJ or STL made in the mount's frame - +x out of the lenses, +y along the baseline, lenses on its mid-line, metres; none: a box about the lenses) and the stereo sensor its child on the lenses' axis, 1 mm before its front. On a face of a shape: its back on the face, looking out, welded to the shape when that moves. Free: fixed at position, looking at look_at, its baseline level. Answers the housing's, the sensor's and the weld's ids
ops.name: assembly_camera

ops.help: Inverse kinematics as a question, nothing moved: whether the effector's frame can reach a point with a turn (as assembly_reach takes them), the errors left, the manipulability (zero at a singularity) and each limited joint's room to its nearest limit, the least of them tightest_room (m or rad)
ops.name: assembly_can_reach

ops.help: The mechanism checked before it plays (the scene untouched): a joint whose links are not where it holds them (a locked freedom off zero: its coordinate, mm or degrees), a joint with a link gone, bodies of a mechanism whose bounding boxes cross by more than 5 mm. Answers clean (nothing found; the answer's own ok only says the check ran) and problems: kind (joint_apart, joint_link, overlap), id, with (the other body), text
ops.name: assembly_check

ops.help: An assembly studied before one's own is built - how a ready car, arm or stand is made: its bodies as a tree of joints with shapes, masses and roles, the drives, motors, sensors and batteries, in words as scene_describe gives the scene (by its name, assembly_list, or a file); nothing is put into the scene
ops.name: assembly_describe

ops.args: {joint: int | joints: [int], dof?: tx|ty|tz|rx|ry|rz, kind?: servo|velocity|dcmotor, stiffness?: number (N m/rad or N/m), damping?: number (N m s/rad or N s/m), target?: number (rad or m), velocity?: number (rad/s or m/s), force?: number (N m or N), voltage?: number (V), resistance?: number (ohm), constant?: number (N m/A), on?: bool}
ops.help: A drive on a joint's freedom (none: its main one - a hinge's turn, a slider's travel), its output a generalised force the robot's own code puts on the joint: servo (stiffness > 0, damping, target, velocity, force), velocity motor (velocity, force) or DC motor (voltage, resistance, constant; a driver feeds it: assembly_power); a turn in rad and N m, a travel in m and N. The kind: as given, else as the fields given say (stiffness or target: servo; voltage, resistance or constant: DC motor), else the drive's own. Fields not given keep their values; the answer gives the drive as it now stands; joints: several at once, in the same step of a running scene (a gripper's fingers)
ops.name: assembly_drive

damping.description: number (N m s/rad or N s/m)

ops.help: An incremental encoder on the joint's main freedom. A line gives four quadrature counts. reference explicitly supplies the calibrated joint coordinate at count zero, in rad or m; omitting it leaves absolute position unreferenced. No automatic homing or true-pose lookup.
ops.name: assembly_encoder

ops.help: A goal for an effector: a see-through cube around it, at its pose; moving or turning the cube drives the effector there by inverse kinematics, the chain's servos following (a window's gizmo moves it while the scene plays)
ops.name: assembly_goal

ops.help: A goal put at a pose at once: a position (world metres) and a turn - Euler degrees, or a quaternion; what is left out stays. While the scene plays the arm leads its effector there in a straight line (a controller's linear move) and its servos hold it - a script's way to try the arm's IK and how it settles; a goal walking a path leaves it. Answers the goal's position and turn
ops.name: assembly_goal_pose

ops.args: {goal: int, close?: bool, force?: number, open_force?: number, travel?: number}
ops.help: A gripper closed (close: true, the default) or opened: each finger - a slider on the effector of the IK goal given (or of the effector itself) - slides to its far end with its drive capped at force N (default 2), so it stops on what it meets and presses with that force; opening, back to its near end with open_force (default 40); travel: to that many metres from open, capped at force (a wheel's step). All the fingers in one step
ops.name: assembly_grip

ops.args: {a: int, b: int, type?: 'hinge'|'weld'|'slider'|'ball'|'cylinder'|'universal'|'planar'|'shock', anchor: [x,y,z], axis?: [x,y,z]}
ops.help: A joint between two shapes (b 0: the world) at a world point along a world direction (a shock: a slider whose spring and damper carry a weight at 4 Hz, damping ratio 0.5 - a's when b is fixed or the world, else the heavier one's shared by its shocks, the earlier ones set to the new share unless changed by hand). A shape that is geometry only becomes a body - a, the moving link, rigid; b, what it hangs on, rigid and fixed - since a joint holds bodies; the answer's note says which
ops.name: assembly_joint

ops.help: The assemblies (сборки) - parts of scenes kept as scene files, a car, a gripper, a stand: the program's own and the user's (assembly_save), each its name and file
ops.name: assembly_list

ops.args: {goal: int, points: [[x,y,z], ...], turns?: [[rx,ry,rz] degrees, ...] | quaternions?: [[w,x,y,z], ...], speed?: m/s, loop?: bool, smooth?: bool, start?: [x,y,z], start_turn?: [rx,ry,rz] degrees | start_quaternion?: [w,x,y,z], turn_length?: m a radian (a turn walked as so much length)}
ops.help: A goal's trajectory: from where the goal stands through the points (world metres) at a speed, while the scene plays - from the start, or from the moment it is set; held at the end, or round again (loop). Each point may have a turn: between two points the goal turns by slerp in step with its travel; smooth: a camera's flight - a centripetal Catmull-Rom spline through the points at constant speed, the turns by SQUAD. The arm follows by inverse kinematics every frame. A new path starts where the last one ends, or at start (turned start_turn): a way re-planned on the walk from where the goal is now (sim_state's goals); no points: the goal stays there. Answers its length and how long it takes
ops.name: assembly_path

turn_length.description: m a radian (a turn walked as so much length)

ops.help: A joint's DC motor fed from a battery: a driver at duty 0 - still until its duty is set (scene_set, robot_command, a controller's duty action, the card's slider); battery 0: the scene's first, or a new 3S pack. Answers the driver's id and its battery's
ops.name: assembly_power

ops.args: {target: int, preset: str, face?: '+x'..'-z', point?: [x,y,z], normal?: [x,y,z], axis?: 0|1|2, flip?: bool, mirror?: bool}
ops.help: Put a ready link (assembly_presets) at a place: wheels, a hinge about the normal, a slider...
ops.name: assembly_preset

ops.help: The ready links in the pie menu's order (clockwise from the top): word, name
ops.name: assembly_presets

ops.args: {target: int, preset: str, face?: '+x'..'-z', point?: [x,y,z], normal?: [x,y,z], axis?: 0|1|2, flip?: bool, mirror?: bool}
ops.help: What assembly_preset would add, without adding it: the new objects' blocks and their joints in the world
ops.name: assembly_preview

ops.args: {effector: int, position: [x,y,z], quaternion?: [w,x,y,z], basis?: [[3],[3],[3]], set?: targets|pose}
ops.help: Inverse kinematics: the effector's frame to a point with a turn (quaternion, or basis - a rotation matrix by rows; none: the point only), the chain from the body it hangs from solved by damped least squares; the coordinates become the targets of the chain's servos (set: pose - the links posed there at once, the servos holding it). Answers whether it reached, the errors left, the coordinates, the joints with no servo
ops.name: assembly_reach

ops.help: The objects ids with all under them and what belongs to them - joints between them, their sensors, drivers and batteries, the controllers that drive only them - kept as the user's assembly of this name (a scene file standing about the origin on the floor). Answers its file
ops.name: assembly_save

ops.args: {target: int, kind: 'imu'|'sonar'|'touch'|'stereo'|'lidar', face?: '+x'..'-z', point?: [x,y,z], normal?: [x,y,z]} | {joint: int, kind: 'wrench'|'effort', dof?: 'tx'..'rz'}, and for an imu, a sonar, a wrench or a lidar model?: str (a row of its table, sensor_models; none: the table's first), spec?: {key: number} over it
ops.help: A sensor put on a thing, no shape of its own: on a face of a shape a sonar looks out of it (x along the normal), an IMU lies flat on it (z out; no face: on top), a touch pad reads the contacts' normal force through it, a stereo camera looks out of it (its two lenses across the face; sensor_capture takes its frame), a lidar sends its pattern of rays out of it - a beam, a ring, a sphere, a narrow grid, by its spec's rays_h, fov_h_deg, rays_v, fov_v_deg (its ring level on a side face); on a joint a wrench reads the force and torque it passes to its link, an effort its drive's force along a freedom
ops.name: assembly_sensor

model.description: str (a row of its table, sensor_models; none: the table's first)

ops.help: Where a link of `size` goes against a face of the target (a face, or the one nearest a world point)
ops.name: assembly_snap

ops.help: The ready link a click most likely means at a place (a face, or point + normal of the polygon hit)
ops.name: assembly_suggest

ops.args: {target: int, side: front_left|front_right|rear_left|rear_right|left|right, model?: bodies|point, suspension?: bool, encoder?: lines (0: none), power?: bool, battery?: int, radius?: m, rolling?: number (C_rr of a point wheel)}
ops.help: A wheel module at a side of a body (forward +x, left -z of its own frame): a shock absorber, a motor wheel whose positive duty drives forward, an encoder counting forward as positive, a driver at duty 0 on the battery
ops.name: assembly_wheel

ops.args: {camera: int, at?: int, point?: [x,y,z], free?: bool}
ops.help: A target camera: it always looks at object `at` (wherever the running world takes it) or at `point`, or (neither) at where it looks now; free: true - a free camera again, looking where it looked
ops.name: camera_aim

ops.help: Every plugin component in the scene (of one type: <plugin>.<component>): its object and values; an instance of a shape is a row too, with its master's values
ops.name: component_list

ops.help: A plugin's component taken off an object
ops.name: component_remove

ops.help: A plugin's component on an object of any kind - a shape, a joint, a light - added if it has none, with these values (a number, [x, y, z], a flag, a word); the plugin's schema says what they mean and draws its card. One undo step
ops.name: component_set

ops.help: A line of an agent's reasoning in the API console, between its calls (changes nothing)
ops.name: console_note

ops.help: Types an operation's call into the API console's input line, letter by letter as a person types (at most 1.2 s), and answers when it is typed; the call itself, sent next, shows in the log as entered from that line - an agent filmed while it works is seen writing each call before it runs. Changes nothing
ops.name: console_type

ops.args: {goal: int, preset?: 'arm', name?: str} | {joint: int, action?: str, speed?: number, name?: str}
ops.help: A controller: for an arm's IK goal (preset 'arm') actions move (across the floor), lift, turn and - when the goal's effector has fingers - grip, bound to W S A D, R F, Z X, Space and the left mouse button, and to a game controller's sticks, right trigger and A; for a joint with a servo one axis action (`action`, default 'move') that moves its target at speed (rad/s or m/s) while its value is held (-1..1). Its actions and bindings are then the scene's data (scene_get / scene_put); controller_input sets its values while the scene runs
ops.name: controller_add

ops.help: The values of a controller's actions while the scene runs, held until set again: a vector2 [x, y] (move: x along the floor's x, y away), an axis or a button a number, -1..1 (lift, turn, grip 0..1); the scene's first controller when no id - the UR5e's panel moves its IK goal and the arm follows
ops.name: controller_input

ops.help: Redo the step undone last. Answers what it changed, as edit_undo
ops.name: edit_redo

ops.help: Undo the last step. Answers what it changed: the objects' ids, whether the world did; undone false: nothing left to undo
ops.name: edit_undo

ops.help: Fires an impulse force now in the running world, as the «Сработать» button does; a constant force acts on its own
ops.name: force_fire

ops.help: The gizmo: its tool (select, move, rotate, scale) and whether its axes are the object's own
ops.name: gizmo_get

ops.help: The gizmo's tool and axes, as the tool shelf sets them (W E R Q, L)
ops.name: gizmo_set

ops.help: The journal's last lines: every change made from the window or the API (where the file is)
ops.name: journal_lines

ops.help: The scene of a session after one of its lines (none: its last) - its last snapshot before, the core edits after it replayed; one undo step
ops.name: journal_restore

ops.help: Every session of the journal: id, start, end, lines, edits, crashed (it did not end and no window holds it)
ops.name: journal_sessions

ops.help: Every operation of the editor: name, help, arguments, their JSON Schema, and kind - query (reads), edit (the scene, one undo step), window (the selection, the view, play and pause: never the authored scene) or action (files, plugins, the program). families: only the operations whose names begin so - ["scene", "sim"] gives scene_* and sim_*; protocol_version - what a client built for it may call: a client of N works with every program of N and later
ops.name: ops_list

ops.help: The plots' recorded history erased, as «Очистить»: the charts stay, empty till the next numbers
ops.name: plots_clear

ops.help: The plots' view (Графики) as one value: view - {arrangement: overlay | lanes | normalized, whole_run, hidden: [chart keys], focus: a chart key alone in the whole width ("": all), time: {axis words: [from, to]} ("": the run's time), values: {chart key: [low, high]}}; charts - every chart: key, section, title, shown; channels - every quantity there is (plots_show puts it on a chart): id, name, unit, value now, shown; presets - the views saved by name (▤, «Раскладка»); words - what is not the plain view. The window's view, no change of the scene
ops.name: plots_get

ops.help: The lines on the plots to a CSV file, as «Сохранить CSV»: the time and a column a line, with its name and unit
ops.name: plots_save

ops.args: {reset?: bool, view?: {…}, preset?: str, save?: str, delete?: str}
ops.help: The plots' view changed, in this order: reset - the plain view (the arrangement kept); view - the whole value as plots_get gives it (a part left out is the plain one); preset - a saved view by name; save - the view as it stands saved by name; delete - a saved view gone. Answered as plots_get. The window's view, no change of the scene
ops.name: plots_set

ops.help: Quantities on the plots, by their ids (plots_get channels): each on the chart of its unit, or a new chart of its own; on false - off every chart. As «Ещё величины…» does. Answered as plots_get
ops.name: plots_show

ops.help: The plugins: name, file, state (работает, запускается, упал, остановлен), last error, commands; folder - where plugin_new makes one, folders - where plugins are looked for (plugin_scan looks again)
ops.name: plugin_list

ops.help: A new plugin from a template in the user's plugins' folder, started: kind command (a command with a field, a button in «Плагины»), controller (a robot's on_tick: its sensors in, joint commands out) or world (an extension of the physics: the bodies in, forces out - wind, a magnet, a thruster)
ops.name: plugin_new

ops.help: A plugin started again (as a save of its file does)
ops.name: plugin_reload

ops.help: The plugins' folders looked through again: a folder with a plugin.py that came since they were is started (a saved plugin.py restarts its plugin by itself, a deleted one is forgotten by itself). With folder - that plugins' folder first added to them and remembered for the next starts: every folder in it with a plugin.py is a plugin (a repository's checkout), as «Плагины → Добавить папку плагинов…»
ops.name: plugin_scan

ops.help: The scene's links as one list, both ways: each {kind, from, to} - kind is the part and the key of the scene file that write it (object.parent, object.instance, goal.effector, target.camera, target.object, pattern.template, link.a, link.b, bridge.joint, bridge.battery, encoder.against, action.target - with its action -, track.object), from the object that holds it, to the object it names (0: the world). from, to, kind: only those - to gives what refers to an object
ops.name: relation_list

ops.help: Commands to the running world, not edits of the scene: a joint's target (its servo, rad or m) or velocity (its velocity motor), a driver's duty (-1..1), a force's strength (a thruster's throttle), held until commanded again; a body's force and torque ([x, y, z] N, N m, world, at its centre of mass) over the next frame. Stop forgets them (the scene as authored is untouched, no undo step, no journal line). E.g. {commands: {"7": {"target": 0.8}, "23": {"force": [0, 2, 0]}}}
ops.name: robot_command

ops.help: Configure bounded API resources transactionally: max_fps in 1..60, idle_timeout_ms in 1000..3600000, max_background_tasks in 1..2. An arm with its camera consumes two tasks. Stop work before lowering a limit below its current use. Status polling does not renew the idle lease.
ops.name: runtime_configure

ops.help: Explicitly renew the resource lease; status polling does not renew it
ops.name: runtime_keepalive

ops.help: Read active API resource usage, limits and monotonic idle lease without renewing it. Limits bound managed work, not operating-system CPU or memory usage.
ops.name: runtime_status

ops.help: Hold managed arms at measured coordinates, stop managed stereo/perception, and pause the host without resetting the authored scene. Releases API work; never kills unrelated applications.
ops.name: runtime_stop

ops.args: {shape: box|sphere|cylinder|cone|plane, name?: str, position?: [x,y,z], size?: [x,y,z], role?: rigid|collider, fixed?: bool, kinematic?: bool, density?: number}
ops.help: A shape as the toolbar's button adds it: in the air over a free spot, named after its shape; role: a moving body (rigid, with its collider) or a static obstacle (collider), as scene_role gives it; fixed: a rigid body held still in the world; kinematic: one that moves as its velocity and spin say and pushes what it meets, itself pushed by nothing; density: a rigid body's kg/m³ (500 unless given; a light crate 150). A cylinder's axis is its own y
ops.name: scene_add

ops.help: A camera at `eye`, looking at `target` (else the scene's centre); kind target: a target camera that always looks there - at object `at` (wherever it goes) or the point
ops.name: scene_add_camera

ops.args: {shape: 'directional'|'radial'|'torque', mode: 'impulse'|'constant', at?: [x,y,z], strength?: number, radius?: m, body?: int}
ops.help: A force as the menu adds it: a push along its own +Y axis or a radial burst or pull, once (impulse) or all the time (constant). A force with no body is a field: it acts on the bodies whose centres are within its radius (a new directional one: 1.5 m; 0: every body) alike, whatever they weigh - strength: m/s of velocity for an impulse, m/s^2 of acceleration for a constant one; a new one stands at 'at' or in the scene centre. body: a directional force made that shape's own - its child at its centre of mass (or at 'at'), acting on it alone at the force's own point, so off the centre it turns the body; its strength is N s or N and, unless given, is sized by the body's mass (an impulse: 3 m/s of velocity; a constant one: 12 m/s^2)
ops.name: scene_add_force

ops.help: A light as the menu adds it: the sun high at a slant, a lamp or a spot over `at` (else the scene's centre); with `position` it stands there shining at `target` (else at `at`)
ops.name: scene_add_light

ops.help: Each shape becomes the hidden template of a row of copies: count of them (5), a step apart (its width and a gap, along x). The row is an object of its own - its pattern line holds the rest (a grid, a circle, a turn a copy: scene_set)
ops.name: scene_array

ops.help: Several edits as one undo step, all or none. A step named by as - {as: "chassis", op, args} - is referred to as "$chassis" (the id it made) or "$chassis.key" (that key of its answer); "$n" is step n from 0. So one batch builds a whole robot: shapes, then the joints, drives and sensors between them, e.g. [{as: body, op: scene_add, args: {shape: box}}, {as: wheel, op: scene_add, args: {shape: cylinder}}, {op: assembly_joint, args: {a: "$wheel", b: "$body", type: hinge}}]
ops.name: scene_batch

ops.args: {id: int, kind?: 'box'|'sphere'|'capsule'|'cylinder'|'mesh', size?: [x,y,z], diameter?: m, height?: m, offset?: [x,y,z], rotation?: [x,y,z], trigger?: bool, ignores?: [str], hulls?: int, concavity?: number}
ops.help: A shape's collider by numbers, apart from what it looks like: the kind; a box's size, a sphere's diameter, a capsule's or a cylinder's diameter and height; its centre (offset) and turn (rotation) on the shape, in the shape's frame. What is not given stays as the collider is now (a fitted one's numbers from the geometry); fitting is off after. What it touches: trigger - a zone that touches nothing and tells what is inside it (sim_state triggers); ignores - the tags (scene_tag) of what it has no contact with. These two alone leave the collider's form as it is. kind mesh - the geometry itself: a body that stands collides by its triangles, hollows and all; a moving one by the mesh cut into convex parts (V-HACD's way): hulls - at most so many (1..64, 32), concavity - how far a part may stand out into the air, a share of the body's diagonal (0.005..0.5, 0.05: CoACD's threshold); cut at once, hulls_made says how many came
ops.name: scene_collider

ops.help: Objects deleted as Del does: with everything under them, the joints and sensors they hold (scene_remove: one object, its children kept)
ops.name: scene_delete

ops.help: The scene in words: the bodies as a tree of joints with their shapes, masses, roles and drives; sensors and where they look; the batteries - for a person or a language model building by text
ops.name: scene_describe

ops.help: Copies a little above the originals (Ctrl+D), or each `by` metres from its original in the world ([0,0,0]: in its place); the copies are the answer
ops.name: scene_duplicate

ops.args: {id?: int, line?: str, key?: str, count?: int}
ops.help: One object's block of the scene file: text, and the same read - kind, name, tags, lines (each line as its words, a number as a number); the whole file without an id, and folder - where its relative file paths (models, textures) are found ("": the program's working folder). With line: values - the count words (1) after key on the object's line that starts with the words of line, as scene_set names them (no key: right after the line's own; null: not there)
ops.name: scene_get

ops.help: A group at the centre of the objects, their poses kept in the world (Ctrl+G)
ops.name: scene_group

ops.help: The objects of the scene: id, kind, name. With kind - only those: a row's kind (entity, group, array, light, camera, joint, battery, driver, sensor, force, wheel, controller, sequence), a sensor's own (encoder, imu, sonar, touch, wrench, effort, stereo), or body - an entity with the rigid role. With tag - only those marked with it (scene_tag); a row says its tags when it has any. What a plugin's field of a scene object chooses from
ops.name: scene_list

ops.help: Objects moved by a step in the world, their angles kept (the gizmo's arrows)
ops.name: scene_move

ops.help: A new scene: the floor and nothing else, the play range 0..10 s (the world's duration)
ops.name: scene_new

ops.help: A scene file opened (one undo step back to the scene before)
ops.name: scene_open

ops.help: A block of the scene file in: a new object (id 0 or unused), or the one of its id replaced
ops.name: scene_put

ops.help: One object out, with its joints; its children keep their place in the world (scene_delete: with everything under it)
ops.name: scene_remove

ops.help: A role given to the shapes or taken from them, as the role bar does; no `on`: switched as a click
ops.name: scene_role

ops.help: The scene saved to a file
ops.name: scene_save

ops.help: Objects scaled by factors along their own axes, a group's spacing too (the cubes)
ops.name: scene_scale

ops.args: {id: int, line: str, key?: str, values?: [number|str]}
ops.help: One 'line key values' of an object's block, as in the scene file (a missing role line is added)
ops.name: scene_set

ops.help: Every hidden object shown again (Alt+H), not the templates of arrays
ops.name: scene_show_all

ops.help: A tag - one word, 'target', 'keep' - put on objects of any kind or taken off them; no `on`: switched. scene_list {tag} finds by it, scene_get says an object's tags. For a plugin or a script to find what it is to act on
ops.name: scene_tag

ops.help: Objects turned about an axis by degrees around a pivot (no pivot: the last object's centre) - the rings
ops.name: scene_turn

ops.help: The groups dissolved, their members kept where they stand (Ctrl+Shift+G)
ops.name: scene_ungroup

ops.help: One kind of block of the scene file as the reader reads it: its lines (parts) - each its first word, what stands between it and its keys (lead), its keys with the form of their values and their unit. What scene_get and scene_set read and write by line and key; the very tables the scene file is read by
ops.name: schema_get

ops.help: The kinds of block the scene file holds - world, physics, entity, group, array, light, force, camera, joint, battery, driver, sensor, wheel, controller, sequence - each with the first words of its lines; schema_get tells one's keys
ops.name: schema_list

ops.help: Run a Python script that builds or changes the scene (import kinetica as ke; scene = ke.connect()) and wait for its end: its edits are one undo step, its print() is the answer's output; a script that falls changes nothing and says its file and line. A script runs and is gone - what stays and extends the editor is a plugin
ops.name: script_run

ops.help: Stop the script that is running (script_run): its process is ended and what it did is taken back, as when a script falls
ops.name: script_stop

ops.help: The selected objects, the active one last
ops.name: selection_get

ops.help: Select these objects as clicks would, the last one active (none: nothing)
ops.name: selection_set

ops.help: The tables of sensor models (data/sensors/<kind>.csv, a row per model as its datasheet states it) and the fields of each kind's datasheet: key, words, unit, range, the value of a sensor no model gave one
ops.name: sensor_models

ops.help: What the scene's sensors read now, as the robot reads them (their datasheets' devices): no truth - the input of a controller. The scene must be running or paused
ops.name: sensor_read

ops.help: A sensor's datasheet: a model's numbers from its table, and numbers given over them (the model's name stays as where they came from; as_model says whether they still are its). Answers the datasheet
ops.name: sensor_spec

ops.help: A sequence: an animation of objects of the scene, kept apart from them (the first one made, or `active`, is the one that plays)
ops.name: sequence_add

ops.help: The objects' tracks removed from the sequence (none named: all of them)
ops.name: sequence_clear

ops.args: {id: int, time: s, sequence?: int, line?: str, key?: str}
ops.help: The object's key at `time` removed (its last: its track goes); with line (and key): that field's key
ops.name: sequence_delete_key

ops.args: {from?: number, to?: number, fit?: bool, curves?: bool, range?: [number]}
ops.help: The Sequencer's view, as F, the wheel and the middle button set it, answered as it stands: from, to - the time in sight, s; fit - the whole sequence again and the values fitted (F); curves - one track's curves (the selected object's) or the tracks; range - the curves' values [low, high] from the bottom to the top ([]: fitted to the curve in sight). Nothing given: only the answer. The window's view, no change of the scene
ops.name: sequence_frame

ops.help: The sequences: each one's id, name, whether it is the Sequencer's and whether ▶ plays it, its playhead, length and loop, and its tracks - the object bound (lost: deleted) and its keys (time s, position m and rotation degrees on its parent)
ops.name: sequence_get

ops.args: {ids: [int], time?: s, sequence?: int, interp?: str, line?: str, key?: str, values?: [number]}
ops.help: A key of each object at `time` (the sequence's playhead when none) where it stands now - its place and turn on its parent (one at the same time replaced); no sequence yet: one is made. The Sequencer's K. With line (and key): that field's numbers instead, as scene_set names it - a colour, a light's intensity, a servo's target (line 'drive rx', key target), a motor's duty (line bridge, key duty) - played between keys too; values: the numbers to key instead of the field's own now
ops.name: sequence_key

ops.args: {id: int, time: s, sequence?: int, new_time?: s, position?: [x,y,z], rotation?: [x,y,z], velocity?: [x,y,z], interp?: str}
ops.help: The object's key at `time` changed: moved to new_time, its place or turn on the parent, how it goes on to the next key (interp: linear, smooth - the cubic through the keys -, step - held), its velocity - the place's slope a smooth key goes through, m/s on the parent; its Bezier handles in the curves, the key ± velocity × a third of the time to the neighbour; given, the key goes on smooth unless interp says else; the bound objects then stand where the sequence has them at its playhead. The Sequencer's curves
ops.name: sequence_key_set

ops.help: The sequence's playhead at `time`: every object it binds to its pose there (in a line between keys, the shortest turn)
ops.name: sequence_seek

ops.args: {sequence?: int, name?: str, loop?: bool, active?: bool, play?: bool}
ops.help: The sequence's name, its loop (past its last key it starts over), whether it is the Sequencer's (active), and whether ▶ plays it when active (play: its bodies led along their tracks; off: shown only, the physics its own)
ops.name: sequence_set

ops.args: {body: positive scene entity id, impulse: [x,y,z] N s, point?: [x,y,z] world metres}
ops.help: Apply one physical world-space impulse in N s to an already built dynamic rigid body addressed by scene entity id. Optional point is in world metres; omitted point applies at the centre of mass. Wakes a sleeping body; adds momentum without teleporting, resetting velocity or editing the graph. Available while playing or paused after sim_step(0). Missing or fixed bodies and malformed or nonfinite commands are refused. Returns only acceptance, not the body's pose or velocity: this is external actuation, not a sensor observation.
ops.name: sim_impulse

ops.help: The plots' channels measured now (the physics engine's truth, for checks): scene - energy of motion, rotation and height, momentum, angular momentum, the deepest contact; objects - each body by entity id: mass, centre, height, velocity, energy, spin, sleep, contact force; group - several bodies as one; joints - each freedom's coordinate (0: the pose the joint was made in), a servo's target, the drive's effort; goals - an IK goal's miss (mm) and turn miss (°). Each channel: id ("<id>/<quantity>"), value, unit, name (the quantity's); names: the asked objects' names by id
ops.name: sim_measure

ops.help: Pause it
ops.name: sim_pause

ops.help: Run the scene (built from the graph)
ops.name: sim_play

ops.help: The Sequencer's take: on - the scene plays (from edit, as ▶) and every dynamic body the playing sequence does not lead is recorded a frame, its pose and velocity, from the world's record_from on (now, if later): before it the world runs and nothing is kept. At the run's end - the world's duration; none: two minutes of take - the take closes and the world pauses (▶ goes on, not recording); it comes in with ■ Stop. Off - the scene stops and the take comes in as a new sequence «Запись N», open, not played by ▶ (a scene_put: one undo step), each body a track of keys at the world's time that give its run back within 0.5 mm and 0.2 degrees (Hermite between recorded keys); a robot's links its joints and IK move are recorded too, bodies that stood still are not; the tracks of the sequence that played come along - a camera's keys, a light's. ■ Stop while recording ends it the same way
ops.name: sim_record

ops.help: The live state: time and frame, every body's pose (position of its frame, rotation: Euler degrees [x, y, z], the turn R = Ry Rx Rz - as the scene file), velocity and spin (asleep: at rest, put to sleep; fixed: a static body; kinematic: one led by its own velocity or by a sequence), every joint's coordinates, main angle or travel, its drive's effort (N m or N) and a DC motor's current and power, every sensor's reading as the robot reads it (its datasheet's device: an IMU's accel and gyro, a sonar's distance, an encoder's count, a wrench's force and torque, a pad's force) with its probe's truth beside it, which entities touch (contacts: a, b - 0 the floor -, points, normal force N, deepest overlap m), what the world could not build (notes); frame_timing: the last 120 frames' mean wall ms in posted commands, the wait for the plugins' on_tick (controllers_ms), the step and the snapshot, and the window's painting - its frames a second, one frame's ms and the renderer, a GPU or llvmpipe (the scene runs slower than the wall clock when they pass frame_dt_ms). The physics engine's truth, for checks - not a robot's sensors
ops.name: sim_state

ops.help: Step N frames (1/60 s each) on pause and answer the live state, as sim_state gives it (frames 0: the scene built as play builds it, its state at time 0); state false: only the time, the frame and the frames stepped - for a client that steps often and reads what it needs by sensor_read or sim_measure
ops.name: sim_step

ops.help: Stop: the scene as it was before play
ops.name: sim_stop

ops.help: Every button and menu item of the window, a panel's own buttons and the visible tabs: text, name, on/off, and for what is shown - an open menu's items too - where it stands: x, y, width, height in the window's picture (the pixels view_screenshot window gives and ui_pointer space window takes): a hand finds it by its name, not by its looks; ui_trigger presses any of them by its text
ops.name: ui_actions

ops.help: A key pressed and released in the 3D view: 'A', '1', 'Escape', 'Delete'... - in an open popup menu first, where Escape closes it; a key the view does not take goes on to the window's shortcuts (F frames the selection), as a real one does; action 'press' holds it down until a 'release' (W A S D fly the view while the right button is held). window: as the window system delivers a real key - the window's shortcuts first, then whatever has the focus (not the view forced); layout 'ru': the key on that QWERTY place typed with the Russian layout on
ops.name: ui_key

ops.args: {action: 'move'|'drag'|'click'|'press'|'release'|'wheel', x: number, y: number, notches?: int, space?: 'view'|'window', button?: 'left'|'right'|'middle', modifiers?: ['shift'|'ctrl'|'alt'], cursor?: bool}
ops.help: The mouse: move to a pixel (drag: with the button held), click / press / release a button there, or turn the wheel there by `notches` (positive: away from the user) - in the 3D view's pixels, or (space 'window') in the whole window's, as its screenshot shows them (an open menu included; a move there shows the tooltip at once). The user's own cursor stays where it is unless cursor: true
ops.name: ui_pointer

ops.help: Press a button or a menu item by its text or name (as ui_actions lists them), a plain panel button by its text or tooltip, or a visible tab by its text
ops.name: ui_trigger

ops.help: Text typed into what has the keyboard focus - a field a click gave it to - as a person types it: each character a key press and release with its text (capitals, digits, Cyrillic, punctuation). Enter, Tab and Escape are ui_key's
ops.name: ui_type

ops.args: {key?: str, line?: [[x,y,z]], segments?: [[x,y,z]], points?: [[x,y,z]], circle?: {}, box?: {}, text?: str, at?: [x,y,z], color?: [r,g,b], colour?: [r,g,b], size?: number, fill?: [str], space?: 'world'|'label'|'screen', turn?: [x,y,z], place?: [x, y], scale?: number, object?: int, stroke?: [r,g,b], stroke_width?: number, leader?: {point?: [x,y,z], end?: 'dot'|'arrow'|'none', place?: 'here'|'aside', grow?: number, pulse?: number, words?: number}, opacity?: number, glow?: number, background?: [r,g,b,a], title?: str, clear?: bool}
ops.help: Lines, points and words over the 3D view in world metres - a plugin's or an agent's picture (a planned path, a force, a sensor's ray, a label), by key: the same key again replaces it, clear takes it off (a key ending in / - all under it; none - all). circle {center: [x,y,z], radius: m, axis?: [x,y,z] (y if none)} - a ring about the axis; box {center: [x,y,z], size: [x,y,z]} - its twelve edges along the world's axes: a gizmo's ring and bounds (centre reads as center, colour as color: the first names, kept). size: a point's width, px (6) - and a label's letters, pt, when larger than plain ones. fill: a flat picture, filled - closed outlines, each a row 'M x y L x y C x1 y1 x2 y2 x y Z' in its own units (x right, y up), painted over the scene. space world (the default): on its own plane at `at`, turned by `turn` (Euler degrees), a unit `scale` metres (1); label: on the screen at the world's point `at`, facing the viewer; screen: in the frame at `place`, fractions of the view from its left top - in both a unit is `scale` of the view's height. object: the picture is that object's and goes where it goes - one in the world lies on it (`at` and `turn` in the object's own frame), a label hangs at `at` from the object's place along the world's axes, above a body however it tumbles; a click on it selects the object. stroke: an edge of that colour round every outline, `stroke_width` of the picture's units wide (0.05) - letters read on any background. leader: a line from the words or the picture to `point` of the part (its own frame, as it turns; no object: the world) - a reference line under them, the line from its nearer end, a dot on the part (end dot), an arrow on its outline (arrow): a drawing's callout, as ISO 128-22 and ГОСТ 2.316 draw them; its grow (0..1, 1) - how much is drawn, from the part, the line, then the reference line -, place aside: laid out every frame with the other callouts so placed - two columns left and right of their points, each in its point's order from the top: no leaders cross -, pulse (0..1) - a ring at the point that phase - and words (0..1, 1) - how much the words or the picture show - are a plugin's to animate it frame by frame. opacity (0..1, 1): the whole drawing's. glow (0..1, 0): a soft halo of its colour round its words, leader and picture; a drawing of only an object (and glow) draws the object itself - its silhouette glows, as the part an agent is building now. background [r,g,b,a]: a plate behind the words, as subtitles have; title: a heading over them in small bold capitals and, with stroke, the plate's edge, an accent bar down its side and the title in that colour - a lower third, a motion design's card. Words in space screen stand at `place`, lines up from it. Drawn while the scene plays: gone at Stop (a key drawn in the edit before stays). Not a scene edit: no undo, no journal
ops.name: view_draw

leader.description: {point?: [x,y,z], end?: 'dot'|'arrow'|'none', place?: 'here'|'aside', grow?: number, pulse?: number, words?: number}

ops.help: The view's camera follows a body's centre of mass whenever the world plays - now, or from the next ▶ - and orbits it as the mouse turns it (Вид → «Следить за выделенным», Shift+F); body 0: the editor's own view again. chase: a chase camera as games make it - no jump, it starts where it looks; going forward, a second after the mouse last turned it, it swings behind the motion (1.2 s, slower under 2 m/s), and aims 0.3 s ahead of the body (Вид → «Камера преследования»); not given: as it was. view_look, view_through, F and Home end it
ops.name: view_follow

ops.help: Show the object (selected), or the whole scene without an id
ops.name: view_frame

ops.help: The view's camera: the eye, the point it orbits, the distance, the vertical field of view
ops.name: view_get

ops.help: The performance plate in the view's lower left corner: the frames a second in large figures coloured by smoothness, the last two seconds of frame times, one frame's paint and the physics' step, the scene's speed against the wall clock, the renderer (a GPU or the processor). on: show or hide it; answers whether it shows and its numbers
ops.name: view_hud

ops.help: The view's camera at an eye, looking at a target (the orbit goes on around the target). glide: seconds to fly there, eased in and out along the orbit, as a smooth view (0: at once); orbit: then it turns about the target that many degrees a second, a turntable, until a person takes the view (a press, the wheel) - a filmed shot
ops.name: view_look

ops.help: The ruler: a line in the view from a world point to another, its length over its middle; answers the length and the difference along x, y and z (metres). None of the two: the line off. Changes nothing of the scene
ops.name: view_measure

ops.help: The pixel of the 3D view (origin top-left) where a world point is seen
ops.name: view_project

ops.args: {file?: str, window?: bool, screen?: bool, width?: int, clean?: bool, marks?: bool, part?: 'view'|'toolbar'|'tools'|'inspector'|'sequencer'|'plots'|'console'|'laboratory'}
ops.help: A PNG of the 3D view (window: the whole window, panels too; screen: the window as a person sees it, its open menus and tooltips painted where they stand and the hand where ui_pointer left it - drawn by the editor, never read from the screen, so no other program's window is in it; width: scaled to so many pixels across, smoothly; clean: without the text and the navigation cube over the view - a picture for the documentation; marks: false - without the editor's own marks in the scene either (joints and their ties, sensors, lights, cameras, the gizmo, the selection's outline): what a camera would film - what a plugin or an agent drew (view_draw) stays in both; view_frame {id} first puts an object in the middle of it; file: where to save it - none, a new file in the temporary folder, named in the answer; a picture of the window answers where the view stands in it, `view` in its pixels; part: one part of the window - the 3D view, the top bar, the tool shelf, a panel -, cut out of the window's picture)
ops.name: view_screenshot

ops.args: {drawings?: bool, cards?: bool, labels?: bool, marks?: bool}
ops.help: What the view shows besides the scene, by kind, as Blender's Overlays switches: cards - what plugins and agents stand in the frame (view_draw: a step's card, a title, an object's glow); labels - what they stand in the scene (formulas, leaders, words over the parts, a plugin's lines); drawings - both; marks - the editor's own marks (joints and their ties, sensors, lights, cameras, the gizmo, the selection's outline, colliders' wireframes): off, the view is what a camera would film. The ruler and motion paths always shown. The tool shelf's three eyes. Answers what shows
ops.name: view_show

ops.help: The view looks through a camera of the scene - its eye, its turn and its lens, wherever its keys or the running world take it - as «Смотрю через» in the view's corner; no camera (or 0): the editor's own view again, as it was
ops.name: view_through

ops.help: The world's 'world' and 'physics' lines of the scene file: text. With line (world, physics): values - the count words (1) after key on that line, as scene_get reads an object's (null: not there)
ops.name: world_get

ops.args: {text?: str, line?: str, key?: str, values?: [number|str]}
ops.help: The world's 'world' and 'physics' lines, as world_get gives them (gravity, box, the play range's end 'duration' in s - 0: none -, the take's start 'record_from' in s, before it, physics engine; a missing physics line: defaults) - or one 'line key values' of them, as scene_set sets an object's: line physics, key substeps
ops.name: world_set
